Text: A shuttle was caught trespassing in {PlayerHouse}’s territory

Security search the vessel, and find a case stamped with the seal of the pre-Collapse Interstellar Authority. Inside are ancient microchips: brain implants, according to your scientists.

The pilot, {d(Courier)}, must be a courier for {d(Ruler)}, {his(Courier)} liege.
“My thanks for handling {Courier}’s trespass diplomatically. I’m sending you some of those microchips: we found a whole cache, so we can spare a few.”
Send {him(Courier)} on {his(Courier)} way, but confiscate the implants
Kill the courier; seize the implants
{D(PlayerCharacter)} killed {Courier} for a case of ancient memory implants

They seem to store memories, which can be accessed once implanted in the skull. 

Most are blank, but one is already written to. According to the technical notes, it holds memories of old Earth.
Accessible from any House member's action menu.
Implant this chip in a House member, granting them long-lost memories of pre-Collapse Earth.
{PlayerCharacter} implanted a pre-Collapse memory from Earth into {TargetCharacter}
A forest in spring. The spray of surf. The cry of a lone hawk. The stormy drumming of non-acidic rain.
{PlayerHouse} confronts you over your memory implant technology

“Irresponsible, experimental technology!” 

“What memories have you given us?"

"Are mine even real!”
I'll destroy all research on them
Your scientists finish studying the memory-implant chips

“We’ve discovered how to fabricate memories and write them to these chips, which can then be implanted in a subject and recalled just as if they were true memories. Imagine: you could make someone believe they owe you their life! Just beware: a traumatic memory requires weeks of preparation, or the mind rejects it.”

“What of pre-Collapse memories? Earth’s forests and beaches?” you ask.

The scientist sighs. “With what source material? There are no forests on this station.”
It would be easy to sedate a House member and implant a memory without their knowledge. Distant rulers are trickier, but perhaps if you invited them to a gathering...
I must remember: traumatic memories require significant preparation...

“But instead of leaving me to suffocate, {firstName(PlayerCharacter)} stopped the fight and offered me an oxygen mask! If not for that, I might have died.”

In the horrific descriptions, you recognise the memories you implanted.

People have called these accusations into question, however. There are inconsistencies.
“I remember, around that time, {Wrongdoer} was acting strangely…”
The final memory has been installed

Planted like silicon seeds.

Does it matter if they never happened? If everyone but you believes they did, what difference does it make?
Implant a memory of {Wrongdoer} committing a crime against {TargetCharacter}
